column1: # Performance acceptance manifest (sub-plan 05, Task 1.1; ARCH-09, DEC-001).
# from the frozen baseline receipt named below, tests/manifests/matrix.tsv and
# tests/manifests/workloads.tsv. Never edit by hand: check-manifest, compare and
# summarize re-derive it from the receipt and refuse any difference. It may tighten
# the receipt's rules, never loosen them, and never drops a frozen class.
# Rows (tab-separated), parsed as data by tests/reports/perf-acceptance.py:
#   provenance <key> <value>        receipt id and sha256 of its BL-TARGETS.txt
#   rule       <name> <text>        frozen rules verbatim, then this task's tightenings
#   unmeasured <class> <reason>     a class the sample schema cannot separate

column3: per cell and workload, a candidate timeout_rate must not exceed the baseline timeout_rate
per platform, at least one previously problematic cold/idle/post-wake class improves beyond measured variability (interleaved runs, same workload)
no latency target is met by weakening TLS, DNSSEC or the no-direct-resolver guarantees
tightening: per cell and workload, the candidate failure count (timeout, SERVFAIL, REFUSED, error) must not exceed the baseline failure rate either, so timeouts traded for fast failures never pass
a workload without a frozen row is compared with a baseline arm measured interleaved in the same session; without that arm it is blocked
tightening: a cold/idle/wake class whose candidate median is slower beyond measured variability fails, so one problem class is never bought with another
per cell, the candidate p95_all_us of a frozen workload must not exceed its platform target
an arm below its budget is insufficient, never pass

baseline and candidate arms of one workload alternate in time: ordered by utc_start, no same-arm run exceeds ceil(n_arm/min_blocks) samples and each arm forms at least min(min_blocks, n_arm) runs; otherwise the comparison is refused
one cache_class per workload, never pooled; NXDOMAIN answers are answered queries and their share is reported per arm

exact percentile bootstrap (no resampling noise, no seed) of the difference of nearest-rank medians, baseline minus candidate; each arm resampled independently; every failed attempt ranks worst (+inf)
P(gain <= 0) < alpha_family/comparisons_per_platform (one-sided, Bonferroni over every cell x problem class of a platform)
tests/reports/stats.sh: supported when attempted*(100-p)/100 >= 10, else exploratory
nice-dns-sample/1 has no stale-answer marker (no TTL, EDE or flag column): a serve-stale answer is indistinguishable from a fresh one, so no stale class is measured or claimed
